newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-LEADING CANDIDATES FOR ITALY COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEADING CANDIDATES FOR ITALY COACH.

text.p: Leading candidates for the post of Italy coach following the resignation of Arrigo Sacchi:

CESARE MALDINI -- Aged 64. The Italy under-21 coach. A former national captain who played for AC Milan, like his son Paolo who now captains Italy and plays for Milan. Has an excellent record as under-21 coach, winning the European title three times but failing at 1996 Atlanta Olympics. That reverse cost him some kudos in Italy but his team has recently been providing far more exciting performances than senior squad. Widely seen as a stopgap rather than permanent replacement but increasingly the favourite, particularly if a longer-term candidate proves unavailable until end of season. An in-house solution would be in keeping with pre-Sacchi days.

DINO ZOFF -- 54. Former national goalkeeper who captained Italy to 1982 World Cup triumph. Most capped player in Italian soccer history (112). Currently president of serie A club Lazio, whose recent league form has been dismal. Federation chairman-elect Luciano Nizzola, who will make decision on replacement for Sacchi after his election on December 14, is a great admirer although Zoff's coaching record is not impressive. Lazio could also be calling increasingly on Zoff's services in coming months, possibly as stand-in for Bohemian coach Zdenek Zeman whose tenure looks more and more in danger.

NEVIO SCALA -- 49. Former Parma coach. Lacks playing pedigree of above two, with just two appearances in Italy B team, but has far stronger record as a club coach. A cultured, opera-loving man, he took Parma to UEFA Cup win in 1995 and Cup Winners' Cup in 1993. Left the club at end of last season without job to go to. Immediately available.

GIOVANNI TRAPPATONI -- 57. Most successful league coach in Italian soccer and therefore always invoked at times of need. Played for AC Milan and found further fame as coach of Juventus and Internazionale. Won league title seven times as a coach (six with Juve). Failed on his last outing in Italy, leaving Cagliari during last season. But has since taken Bayern Munich back to top of German Bundesliga. Long shot because of likely contractual problems.

FABIO CAPELLO -- 50. Sacchi's successor at AC Milan and every bit as successful. In first season at helm of Spanish league leaders Real Madrid. Played for national team 32 times. Took AC Milan to four league titles in five years and European Cup in 1994. Looks a very long shot but has been mentioned as a candidate in recent media reports.
